CausalChain: FGF19 overexpression → Enhanced FGFR4 signaling → Increased tumor cell proliferation and establishing immunosuppressive TME; Overexpression of PCSK9 → LDLR degradation on CD8⁺ T cells → Impaired TCR recycling and reduced T cell activation; Inhibition of FGFR4 → Reduction in tumor growth and TME immunosuppression; Blockade of PCSK9 → Restoration of LDLR levels → Enhanced TCR recycling and T cell function; Combined effect → Synergistic improvement in antitumor immunity and sensitivity to checkpoint blockade.
Hypothesis: Dual inhibition of FGFR4 and PCSK9 will synergistically restore antitumor immunity by simultaneously suppressing tumor proliferation and enhancing CD8⁺ T cell function, thereby overcoming resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors in hepatocellular carcinoma.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) represents a complex malignancy in which multiple oncogenic pathways and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment contribute to disease progression and therapeutic resistance. Recent insights have revealed that an overactive FGF19‐FGFR4 signaling axis not only drives tumor proliferation but also shapes an immune hostile milieu, while emerging data indicate that PCSK9 impairs antitumor immunity by reducing low‐density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR)‐mediated T cell receptor recycling in CD8⁺ T cells. Based on these findings, we propose a novel dual-targeting strategy that combines FGFR4 inhibition with PCSK9 blockade to simultaneously suppress tumor cell proliferation and rejuvenate T cell mediated immune responses. This integrated approach may synergistically enhance the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in HCC.
